samples.question: The picture is one patch bay. On the left there are five square coloured pads, one per row; on the right there are five identical dark square sockets. Five grey cables of identical colour and thickness each join exactly one pad to exactly one socket, and every socket is used exactly once. Each cable runs as a staircase of horizontal and vertical straight runs. Where two cables meet, one passes over and the other passes under: the cable underneath is drawn with a small white break, and it continues on the far side of the crossing cable in the same straight run, in the same row or column. A break is therefore never the end of a cable; a cable ends only at a pad or at a socket. Exactly one socket is outlined by a magenta frame. The rows are not wired straight across: the pad in the framed socket's own row is never the answer, and the cables carry no colour, thickness, or style information about which pad they come from. Follow the cable that leaves the framed socket, turning at every corner and continuing straight through every break, back to the pad it comes from. What is the colour of that pad? Answer red, orange, purple, blue, green or teal.
